transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

For Samsung washer dryers like your WD90T534DBW, drying sends fluff and condensed water out through the pump. A clogged pump filter at the bottom front stops this process, which can cause the water to back up and leak. Please switch the machine off and unplug it first. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Unscrew the filter slowly so the water comes out gradually. You may refer to the picture shown in the app for guidance. Was the filter full of fluff or debris (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the pump filter is" — The pump filter is usually behind a flap at the bottom front. Turn the machine off and drain any water first, then twist the filter out to clear it. Typical location — your machine may differ.]
I haven't checked the filter yet. The drum gets properly hot during drying and the clothes come out warm but damp, so I don't think it's a drainage problem. Is there anything else it could be?

Thanks for letting me know. No problem if you haven’t had a chance yet. Drying sends fluff and condensed water out through the pump, so a clogged pump filter at the bottom front stops drying and can make water back up and leak. Switch the machine off and unplug it first. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Unscrew the filter slowly so the water comes out gradually. Was the filter full of fluff or debris (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

I still haven't checked it, and the assistant repeated itself rather than answering my question. Is there anything else it could be, like how I'm using it? It's a full 9kg drum that I wash and dry in one go, if that matters.

Thanks for letting us know about the issue during drying. It is worth noting that a washer-dryer can typically only dry about half the load it washes—for example, 8 kg washed might result in just 5 kg dried. Attempting to dry a full wash load often leaves clothes damp, which is a very common cause of this problem. Please check the specific dry capacity listed on the front of your machine or in the user manual to see if you have exceeded it. Was the load more than the dry capacity (and have you split it), or was it within the dry capacity?

The manual says 6kg for drying, and I was putting in a full 9kg drum, so yes, it was over the dry capacity. I haven't split it. I also often turn the spin down to 800 to reduce creasing, if that matters.

Thanks for letting us know about the issue during drying. Please run a drying programme using a load that fits within the dry capacity, and keep an eye on it while it runs. Is it working properly now, or is the problem still there?
I tried a half-drum load with the spin on full and it came out dry. So it seems to be the load size, or maybe the spin setting.

[Heading: Drying load bigger than the dry capacity]
Thanks for letting us know. I am glad to hear it is working normally again. A drying load bigger than the dry capacity was the likely cause. No part is needed.
